SLIIT Research Project / R26-IT-145

Smart Camp Box

An Integrated IoT and Artificial Intelligence Framework for Safety, Communication, Learning Assistance, and Resource Optimization in Disaster Relief Camps

A single portable, offline-first box that predicts flood and landslide risk at each camp, gates educational content for displaced children by psycho-attentional readiness, and keeps critical messages flowing over degraded networks.

02 / Domain

Research Context

Three operational failures persist in disaster relief camps — site-level hazard warnings, children's learning readiness, and reliable communication. The Smart Camp Box addresses all three from one platform.

Literature Survey Research Gap Research Problem Research Objectives Sub-Objectives Methodology Technologies Used

Literature Survey

Environmental risk monitoring. IoT sensor networks and GIS-based watershed analysis are well established for regional flood warning. However, most systems report district-level risk from accumulated rainfall rather than evaluating whether one specific camp location will be covered by rising water. Combining GPS-derived altitude with Digital Elevation Models for camp-level inundation checks remains underexplored.

Education in disaster contexts. Trauma-induced neurological suppression directly impairs children's attention, memory and academic learning. Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025) affected 890,000 children and damaged 1,682 schools with teacher-to-student ratios reaching 1:77 — yet no AI-driven educational system was part of the emergency response. Existing platforms assume the learner is psychologically ready.

IoT communication under constraint. MQTT is the dominant lightweight protocol for IoT, but standard deployments assign static QoS levels at configuration time. Uniform QoS in constrained gateways cannot distinguish life-critical biometric data from routine telemetry precisely when bandwidth collapses.

Research Gap

G1

Regional warnings, not site-specific risk

Existing monitoring systems stop at regional granularity — no unified platform fuses live telemetry, external river data, DEM terrain features and ML into a per-camp flood and landslide probability.

G2

Readiness is assumed, never measured

No educational system deployed in an emergency applies an automated, per-session psycho-attentional gate before delivering curriculum content, or monitors children for persistent welfare distress.

G3

Static QoS in dynamic degradation

MQTT QoS is fixed at configuration time. Nothing adapts message priority to real-time network state, so critical registration and distribution data can be lost under severe constraints.

Research Problem

Disaster relief camps face three persistent operational challenges simultaneously: camp-level flood and landslide prediction, psychological and attentional readiness assessment for displaced children, and resilient communication under degraded network conditions.

Current systems solve these in isolation — and many depend on stable Internet connectivity that disaster environments cannot guarantee. The result is delayed evacuation decisions, ineffective educational delivery for traumatised learners, and loss of critical operational messages at the worst possible moment.

Research Objectives

To design, develop and evaluate the Smart Camp Box — a portable, offline-first IoT framework that tightly couples a location-aware environmental risk monitoring engine, the Psycho-Attentional Gated Educational System (PAGES), and the Semantic-Aware Adaptive Message Prioritization (SAAMP) framework into a single platform for disaster relief camp operations.

Sub-Objectives

SUB-SYSTEM 01

Location-Aware Risk Monitoring

Continuously assess flood and landslide risk at each individual camp in real time.

  • GPS/GNSS altitude + DEM risk profiling
  • Multi-sensor telemetry & watershed analysis
  • ML risk model with automated threshold alerts
  • Centralized multi-camp dashboard
SUB-SYSTEM 02

PAGES Learning Gate

Assess and support the cognitive readiness of Grade 3–4 children (ages 7–9) per session.

  • Three-source behavioural fusion scoring
  • Binary readiness gate with calming re-assessment
  • NIE-aligned content delivery
  • Two-phase welfare anomaly detection
SUB-SYSTEM 03

SAAMP Communication

Guarantee prioritized delivery of critical operational data on constrained networks.

  • Biometric registration & wristband identity
  • Source-Action criticality classification
  • Predictive network-state monitoring
  • Adaptive MQTT QoS + priority buffering

Methodology

Field & literature grounding

Design Science Research cycle: literature review across three domains plus a primary field interview at the Kolonnawa Divisional Secretariat on camp safety requirements.

Build the sub-systems

Three tightly coupled modules — risk prediction, PAGES gating, and SAAMP message prioritization — developed in parallel by the three researchers.

Integrate on the box

Modules converge on Smart Camp Box hardware: ESP32 sensor node, Raspberry Pi 5 edge server, solar power, and MQTT bridging to the cloud dashboard.

Evaluate against targets

Historical disaster validation for risk predictions, a 20–30 student pilot for PAGES, and simulated network-degradation benchmarks for SAAMP.

03 / Sub-systems

Three Tightly Coupled Modules

Each sub-system is owned by one researcher and plugs into the same portable box. Select a card to open its objectives and measurable outcomes.

Onboard sensors
Key objectives
  • GPS/GNSS-based location detection with latitude, longitude and altitude for elevation-based risk profiling.
  • Real-time measurement of rainfall intensity, soil moisture, ground movement and humidity at each camp.
  • Geospatial watershed and upstream-flow analysis via QGIS and OpenStreetMap to identify direct water paths.
  • External data integration — river water levels, gauging stations and weather forecasts — with a proximity-based station matcher.
  • Weighted ML fusion model estimating flood and landslide probability with automated threshold alerts.
  • Cloud dashboard aggregating live risk levels across all registered camps for evacuation decisions.

Gate accuracy target
>90%
NIE alignment
0.75
Alert precision
Key objectives
  • Three-source behavioural fusion: gamified inhibitory-control task (50%), passive interaction signals (30%) and rolling historical baseline (20%) scored 0–100.
  • Binary readiness gate thresholded at 55/100, with a structured calming breathing activity and automated re-assessment on failure.
  • Standardized cognitive content layer aligned to the National Institute of Education Grade 3–4 curriculum.
  • Two-phase anomaly detection — Z-score thresholding from session three, then per-child Isolation Forest on AWS Lambda.
  • Welfare alerts on three consecutive flagged sessions, or three flags within the most recent five.
  • Full offline operation on Raspberry Pi 5 with dual-mode AP+STA Wi-Fi and automatic cloud sync.

Network-state class.
Key objectives
  • Pre-disaster fingerprint registration (R307) with wristband barcode issuance for duplication-free entitlements.
  • Source-Action Classification Schema assigning Critical / Important / Routine criticality across six system sources.
  • Real-time network monitor classifying connectivity as Good, Weak, Poor or Offline from latency and packet loss.
  • Random Forest predictor forecasting network quality 60 seconds ahead for proactive QoS adjustment.
  • Priority buffer with critical-first flushing when connectivity is re-established.
  • Offline awareness module serving video to 20+ devices and WebSocket announcements in under 2 seconds.
